src.t: General Pathology I MCQs & Short Answers
Chemical Pathology and Haematology Exam Review

ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Intracellular protein synthesis converts DNA instructions into functional proteins via transcription and translation. Errors can cause metabolic disorders, cancers, and infectious disease complications.

sections.p: Protein synthesis is the cellular process of making proteins from amino acids using mRNA templates. Diagnosis of defects relies on clinical clues and laboratory tests of gene or protein function.
b: Transcription: DNA → mRNA
Translation: mRNA → polypeptide
Post‑translational modifications complete functional proteins

sections.p: Disruption can be genetic, infectious, nutritional, or toxic.
b: Inherited mutations (e.g., ribosomopathies, mitochondrial DNA defects)
Viral hijacking of host translation (HIV, hepatitis B)
Severe protein‑calorie malnutrition
Antibiotics that inhibit ribosomes (chloramphenicol, aminoglycosides)
Heavy metal poisoning (lead, mercury)

sections.p: Patients may show growth failure, anemia, neuro‑developmental delay, or organ‑specific dysfunction depending on the protein affected.
b: Failure to thrive in infants
Macrocytic anemia from impaired hemoglobin synthesis
Neuropathy from defective myelin proteins

sections.p: When advanced tests are not accessible, clinical scoring and basic labs (CBC, liver enzymes) guide suspicion.

t.b: Detects accumulation or deficiency of specific amino acids; abnormal patterns suggest enzyme blocks in synthesis.
Shows whether transcription of a gene is reduced; low levels point to transcriptional defects.
Assesses translation efficiency; decreased activity indicates ribosomopathy or drug toxicity.
Identifies pathogenic mutations; confirms inherited disorders when other tests are unavailable.

sections.p: Uncorrected synthesis defects can lead to irreversible organ damage or death.
b: Rapidly progressive neurodegeneration
Severe metabolic acidosis
Life‑threatening infections due to immune protein deficiency

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause, support protein production, and monitor complications.
b: Nutritional supplementation with essential amino acids when deficiency is present
Antiviral therapy for viral hijacking (e.g., tenofovir for HBV) to restore host translation
Remove ribosome‑inhibiting drugs; switch to safer alternatives
Chelation therapy for heavy metal poisoning to free ribosomal sites

sections.p: Regular monitoring of growth, neurodevelopment, and laboratory markers ensures early detection of relapse or new deficits.
b: Quarterly growth and developmental assessments in children
Annual CBC and liver function tests
Genetic counseling for families with inherited defects

sections.p: Conditions that mimic protein synthesis failure.
b: Primary malabsorption syndromes (celiac disease) – cause nutrient loss, not synthesis machinery
Mitochondrial disorders – affect energy, not directly translation

sections.p: Laboratory values may appear normal despite functional deficits.
b: Normal serum protein levels can mask defective specific proteins (e.g., immunoglobulins)
Transiently normal amino acid profiles after recent feeding

whenToSeekHelp: Rapid weight loss and failure to thrive in infants

faq.q: Why does a viral infection affect protein synthesis?
faq.a: Viruses use host ribosomes to make viral proteins, often shutting down normal cellular translation.

faq.q: Can protein synthesis defects be cured?
faq.a: Some are treatable with nutrition or removing toxins; genetic forms may require lifelong management or gene therapy.

faq.q: What basic test can hint at a synthesis problem in low‑resource settings?
faq.a: A complete blood count showing macrocytic anemia suggests impaired hemoglobin protein production.

exam: Explain how a mutation in a ribosomal protein gene leads to anemia and growth failure.
List three reversible causes of impaired intracellular protein synthesis and their management.
Interpret a serum amino acid profile showing elevated phenylalanine in the context of protein synthesis disorders.
